concerns.location: research.md:1 Dataset Strategy table, GSN row
concerns.text: The 'verified' GSN URL is https://huggingface.co/datasets/Francesco/construction-safety-gsnvb/... — the repository name indicates a construction-safety dataset, not a Group Sunspot Number series. The plan itself demonstrates that other URLs in the same verified block were content mismatches (Ethereum/chat/Amazon). The plan asserts 'monthly historical sunspot record — satisfies FR-001' without evidence the file contains date + sunspot variables. If this is a wrong-dataset, the primary predictor for the entire project is invalid; the plan must verify the actual columns/content of this parquet before building on it, or the GSN source is a dataset-variable-fit failure.

concerns.location: research.md:1 Dataset Strategy table, CMIP6 row
concerns.text: The CMIP6 source is a 'wip_cmip6' test shard (test-00000-of-00012.parquet) with key variables listed as 'time, solar forcing / TSI variable' — the slash suggests uncertainty about whether a TSI/solar-forcing variable actually exists in this shard. FR-010/FR-011 depend on a CMIP6 v3.2 solar-forcing TSI series; the plan should confirm the shard contains that variable (and at what temporal resolution/coverage, e.g. whether it spans 1610–present for the minima comparisons) rather than assuming it.

concerns.location: plan.md:Summary item (3) and Phase 3/5; research.md §2.1 'Cycle-Agnostic fallback'
concerns.text: With no verified TSI dataset, the Cycle-Agnostic fallback (GSN-only RF/GP mapping GSN→TSI) also has NO training target — a GSN-only feature set still requires TSI labels to fit any regressor. Yet Phase 5 states the fallback 'produces the reconstruction' with 95% prediction intervals. As written, the reconstruction output (FR-004, tsi_reconstruction_1610_2002.parquet) is infeasible: there is no data resource from which any GSN→TSI mapping can be learned. The plan must either identify a verified TSI training source or state that FR-004/FR-005/SC-003 outputs cannot be produced at all (not merely 'degraded'), and flag this at the spec level.
